temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small florets, bite-size 375°F / 190°C · 6 min 400°F / 205°C · 8 min Medium florets, about 1½ inches 375°F / 190°C · 8 min 400°F / 205°C · 11 min Large florets or halved heads 375°F / 190°C · 10 min 400°F / 205°C · 13 min Burnt tips, hard stems A broccoli floret is two foods joined together. The top is a cluster of tiny, dry buds with a huge surface area, and in moving hot air those buds lose their water in minutes, crisp, then blacken and taste bitter. The stem below is dense and wet, and it needs several minutes more to go tender. Cook a floret whole and you end up choosing between charred tips with a crunchy raw stalk or a soft stalk under burnt crumbs. The fix is in the knife work. Cut florets with short stems, and split thick stems lengthways so every piece has a thin stalk. Peel and slice the main stalk into coins; it is sweet once cooked. The other problem is weight: dry florets are so light that the fan can lift small pieces into the heating element, so toss them in oil first. Worked example One medium head of broccoli cut into 1½-inch florets with the stems split, tossed with a tablespoon of olive oil, salt and garlic. Preheat 4 minutes, cook at 375°F for 8 minutes and shake once halfway. Bite-size florets are done in about 6 minutes; large ones in about 10. Roasted on a tray in a conventional oven, the same head takes 400°F for around 11 minutes. How to tell it is done The tips should be browned at the edges, with a few crisp dark spots, while the rest of the floret stays bright green. Pierce a stem with a knife: it should slide in with slight resistance. Grey-green florets that have gone soft were overcrowded and steamed; black, bitter tips mean the pieces were too big for the time or sat without oil. Before it goes in Wash the broccoli well ahead of time and let it dry completely, or spin it in a salad spinner; wet florets steam instead of roasting. Coat every piece evenly with oil, which protects the tips and weighs them down. Add grated cheese or lemon juice after cooking. Do not fill the basket more than one layer deep. About 8 minutes at 375°F for medium fresh florets, shaken once. Small florets take around 6 minutes and large ones around 10. Why does my air fryer broccoli burn? The fine buds on top dry out much faster than the stem softens. Cut smaller florets with thin stems and coat them in oil. Can I air fry frozen broccoli? Yes, but it releases a lot of water and comes out softer. Use frozen mode, which accounts for the extra moisture, rather than this fresh setting. Why did broccoli fly around my air fryer? Dry florets are light enough for the fan to lift. A coat of oil weighs them down and keeps them in the basket. What is the oven equivalent for broccoli? 400°F for around 11 minutes on a tray in a conventional oven.
